Yes, the rationale for a shadowban is so that spammers and bots do not know that they have been incapacitated.

It is very effective against indiscriminate spammers, those that try to post on as many sites as possible. These spammers don’t ever go back to check on their work; they just carpet-bomb blogs and news sites and forums using bots that are only roughly tuned for each site (for example to account for different input fields and formats).

It is also effective against small-time spammers, those who don’t use bots but are just spamming for a personal agenda (like promoting their blog or online shop). They might not notice being shadowbanned for a while.

It is less effective on a spammer who is specifically targeting your site with bots because, as you say, they can check for shadowbans and fine-tune their bots. These are frankly quite rare because if they are proven to be spam, they are easily disabled by other methods (like domain blacklisting), so it’s not worth the effort to target one strong site with bots when they can target 1,000s of weaker sites.
